metadata.rust_flags: release -O3; codegen-units=1; lto=thin; target-cpu=native; no-default-features; rayon; locked
metadata.affinity: OS scheduling, no affinity; persistent exact-size pools; one benchmark process at a time
metadata.parallel_strategy: Both: filter static source row ranges, sum matched counts, allocate one exact-size target, copy disjoint destination row ranges, join. C++ uses its persistent pool and full-row memcpy; Rust uses Rayon and writes three u64 values plus two TextCell<N> values per matched row, including both metadata words. No worker output tables or second payload copy.
metadata.schema: five fields: id u64, selector u64, amount u64, name and message each exactly text_bytes ASCII bytes. GD uses inline bounded string cells including lengths/terminators/alignment; Rust uses three Vec<u64> and two Vec<TextCell<N>>, each repr(C) cell holding a u32 metadata word and [u8; N], N=16 or 128. Same five typed columns in source and target.
metadata.representation_scope: Rust is a benchmark-local typed SoA prototype, not storage supported by the existing dynamic gd::Table.
metadata.rust_text_metadata: one u32 per text cell: high 8 bits tag, low 24 bits valid length; tag=(id%256*17 + column*101)%256; column=0 name, 1 message. Fixture lengths equal N. Validate once on cell construction; copy whole cells without validation; check every copied tag and length outside timing.

ownership.arrays: independent deep-copied integers, metadata words and array bytes

metadata.predicate: selector < percentage; selector = (row%100*37 + row//100*17)%100; exact density per 100 rows
metadata.timing_contract: source construction, pool startup, oracle, full digest outside samples; fresh target allocation, filtering, temporary indices where used, prefix/gather, synchronization, copying and destruction inside; one ordered target; no worker output tables; no sharing, reference counts, per-cell allocations, zero-fill pass or untimed merge
